# Types and Options Reference

Most of what PlussPl lets you change about a figure is a **value** you pass to a `Studio`, `Pane` or `Trace` method: where a legend goes, how an axis is scaled, which grid lines are drawn, how a surface is lit, which colours a theme holds. These value types are the *options* of the plotting API, and this reference documents each one in one place: a table of every value or field with its meaning and default, where it is used, and a rendered demonstration of every value, so you can choose by looking at the result.

Each page explains what the option does, lists its values or fields in a table, then gives examples with their printed output and figures. Every example is compiled and run by `tools/plotdocs.py`, which writes the printed output and figures, so they cannot drift from the code. Examples are shown without the lines around them: each is the body of `main()` in a program that starts with `#include <pluss/pl/plusspl.h>` and `using namespace pluss::pl;`, and `fig.save_svg("figure.svg")` writes the figure shown beneath it.

The per-method pages are in the [Studio](studio_api_reference.md), [Pane](pane_api_reference.md), [Trace](trace_api_reference.md) and [flash](flash_api_reference.md) references; they link here for the meaning of each option value.

## Legends

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`KeyPlace`](api/types/KeyPlace.md) | Where a pane draws its inset legend. |
| [`KeyDock`](api/types/KeyDock.md) | Which edge the figure-wide legend is docked to. |
| [`KeyFrame`](api/types/KeyFrame.md) | How a legend is boxed. |
| [`KeyShape`](api/types/KeyShape.md) | Whether a legend lists its entries in a column or in a row. |

## Axes, scales and grid

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`ScalePolicy`](api/types/ScalePolicy.md) | How an axis maps values: linear, log10 or symlog. |
| [`LimitMethod`](api/types/LimitMethod.md) | How an axis range is fitted to the data. |
| [`TickFormat`](api/types/TickFormat.md) | How tick labels are written. |
| [`GridStyle`](api/types/GridStyle.md) | Which grid lines a pane draws. |

## 3D view and surface appearance

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`Lens`](api/types/Lens.md) | The camera of a 3D pane: angles, projection and field of view. |
| [`LightRig`](api/types/LightRig.md) | The lights of a 3D pane. |
| [`ShadeMode`](api/types/ShadeMode.md) | How a surface is coloured across its cells. |
| [`LightingMode`](api/types/LightingMode.md) | Whether and how a surface is lit. |
| [`MaterialProfile`](api/types/MaterialProfile.md) | How a lit surface responds to light. |

## Colour and themes

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`Rgba`](api/types/Rgba.md) | The colour type. |
| [`PaletteRamp`](api/types/PaletteRamp.md) | A named ramp of colours that values are mapped through. |
| [`Theme`](api/types/Theme.md) | The colours a figure is drawn in. |

## Annotations and geometry

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`RuleCue, BandCue, PinCue`](api/types/Cues.md) | Reference lines, shaded bands and pinned notes on a pane. |
| [`Range1d, Vec3d, Extent2d`](api/types/Geometry.md) | The small value types for a range, a point and a figure size. |

## Trace types and their options

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`TraceKind`](api/types/TraceKind.md) | The kind of drawing a trace is. |
| [`ViolinOptions`](api/types/ViolinOptions.md) | The width, smoothing, scaling, inner mark and side of a violin. |

## Layout and export

| Type | What it chooses |
|---|---|
| [`MosaicLayout, PanePlacement`](api/types/MosaicLayout.md) | How the panes of a figure are arranged on a grid. |
| [`PdfEngine`](api/types/PdfEngine.md) | Which writer produces a PDF file. |
